newsitem.title: USA: N. central Kansas wheat seen on par with last year.
newsitem.headline: N. central Kansas wheat seen on par with last year.

text.p: The wheat crop in north central and east central Kansas has the potential to yield as much as or possibly more than it did a year ago, crop scouts on the Wheat Quality Council hard red winter wheat tour said.

"I don't think there are any surprises," said a grain company wheat marketing specialist. "The potential is to get even bigger (crops) than what we've seen today if we get rain and it doesn't get hot and dry."
In Riley and Clay counties in east central Kansas, the wheat crop is in the "flag" or head-in-boot development stage, the final stage of stem extension before heading.
Wheat stands were rated good to very good and there were virtually no signs of disease, crop scouts reported. Only some wheat streak mosiac was seen in Clay County, they said.
Estimated yields per acre in Riley and Clay couties were 40 to 43 bushels per acre. A year ago those counties produced 40 to 41 bushels per acre.
"It looks as good as last year," a flour buyer for an East Coast bakery said. "Statistically, last year's averages are pretty close to what we're seeing, maybe a little better."
In north central Kansas, in Washington and Republic counties, wheat was also in the flag stage and stands were rated fair to good, crop scouts said.

In that region, the potential yield per acre was estimated in a wide range of 30 to 44 bushels per acre. A year ago, Washington and Republic counties produced 34 bushels per acre, tour participants said.
